units.translation: 1 Etymologicum Genuinum (AB) Πλειάδες (A, -ας B): they are named from Pleione, daughter of Oceanus and wife of Atlas. Pindar (fg 74a Schr.) speaks about their catasterism (A, καταστερισμένου B), [ὡς deleted by Et. M.] that when Pleione was travelling with her daughters through Boeotia, Orion met her. Then, falling in love (Et. M., -έντος AB), he rushed to seize her, and Orion pursued her as she fled with her daughters, and their flight lasted five years (A, five years B) without ceasing. And Zeus (A, Et. M., omitted by AB) on account of their suffering, as it were memorials (αὐτῶν added by B), placed the Pleiades among the stars (Sylburg, καταστερίσθαι AB) as they fled from Orion. 〈or rather from πλειών, added by W〉, which is a year. They are signs of summer and winter. Apollonius, the author of the Argonautica. cf. W 76 sch. Α Σ 486 sch. Pind. Nem. II 17 a. c Athen. XI 490 e Eust. 1155, 48. 1712, 49
1 Πληι- four times in L : Πλει- in P
4 ποτε added after γάρ in P
7 φασιν in P : φησιν in L

230. That the bulls are bronze-footed and breathe fire, Pherecydes (3 fg 112 J.) also says. Lm (P)
10 καὶ before Φ. in P : omitted in L

232a. πρὸς δὲ καὶ αὐτόγυον στιβαροῦ: there are two kinds of ploughs, the compacted and the self-limbed; the compacted is the one that has the share from a joint; the share is the part in which the ploughshare is fitted. The wood extending from the share to the oxen is called the γύης, and the part from the γύης is the ἱστοβοεύς. The parts of the yoke placed on the necks of the oxen are called by some ζεύγλαι, by others μέσσαβα. Eratosthenes in his Architectonicus (fg 17 Strecker) describes the construction of ploughs.
